races.name: EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Hickory Lad
runners_data.note: Front runner with class edge from Thirsk second, will get uncontested lead and first run on rivals.
runners_data.comment: Sets a good standard on his promising debut second at Thirsk 19 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: 18-1, shaped with plenty of promise when second to a short-priced Kevin Ryan runner at Thirsk (5f, good) 19 days ago, pulling well clear of the rest; will set the bar high for a race like this if making the anticipated improvement.

runners_data.name: Kodi Bear Light
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity but Burke stable in excellent form (10/41) and breeding suggests 5f speed could be sharp.
runners_data.comment: Newcomer from a powerful yard and the obvious danger to Hickory Lad
runners_data.spotlight: 28,000euros yearling; seventh foal; closely related to 5f/6f winner Sergeant Pep (including 2yo; RPR 93) and half-sister to winners Transparent (7f/1m AW; 91) and Lafan (1m/9.4f AW; 86); with a very powerful yard and a potential threat to Hickory Lad if the market signals are positive.

runners_data.name: State Of Gold
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who fades in finish, lost shoe excuse from Redcar debut but still needs significant improvement.
runners_data.comment: Well held on recent debut but went off 9-2 so better was seemingly expected
runners_data.spotlight: Reported to have lost her left-hind shoe when weakening to finish well held on last Monday's 5f Redcar debut (good to firm), with her betting prominence (9-2) suggesting better was anticipated.

runners_data.name: Stay On Tab
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who raced too keenly on debut, needs to settle better to avoid another fade.
runners_data.comment: Too keen when well-held sixth on C&D debut
runners_data.spotlight: 33-1, raced keenly just off the pace before fading into a well-held sixth on his soft-ground C&D debut 25 days ago; should stay in contention for longer if he settles better, particularly on this drier surface, but he'll need a big chunk of improvement to get heavily involved.

races.paceDynamic: Hickory Lad will dictate terms from the front with no obvious pace pressure in this small field. State Of Gold and Stay On Tab are likely to race prominently behind him, but neither showed the early pace to challenge for the lead. The lone leader should get comfortable splits through the early stages, setting up a tactical race where positioning matters more than sustained pressure. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid traffic problems in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hickory Lad Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Hickory Lad gets easy early fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The favourite gets first run on his rivals and has enough in hand from his Thirsk second to hold on. His class edge over this field becomes decisive when he's not under pressure early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Kodi Bear Light Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the Burke newcomer shows significant ability on debut and travels strongly
scenarios.body: Kodi Bear Light picks up the pieces late as others fade, with the strong stable form (10/41 in 14 days) suggesting this one is well-schooled. The breeding suggests 5f speed that could be potent fresh.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: State Of Gold Bounces
scenarios.trigger: If State Of Gold settles better and the lost shoe was the main issue at Redcar
scenarios.body: The filly gets a confidence-boosting run in behind Hickory Lad and finds more than her debut effort suggested. Her early market support suggests connections expected better than that eighth place.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stay On Tab Improves
scenarios.trigger: If Stay On Tab settles much better and the step up in ground helps significantly
scenarios.body: The Jardine runner benefits from a more patient ride and the better surface allows him to stay on where he faded badly on soft ground. His keen racing remains the biggest concern.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Hickory Lad gets away with very slow early fractions - could make him unstoppable.
Monitor Kodi Bear Light's market moves as any support would signal Burke confidence.
Check if State Of Gold shows early speed to press Hickory Lad or settles in behind.
Watch Stay On Tab's early tactics - if he races keenly again he'll fade like last time.
Observe if Andrew Mullen drops Stay On Tab out further back to help his settling.

races.name: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap

runners_data.name: Fille Unique
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits, recent Newcastle third showed competitive level, Paul Mulrennan booking suggests stable confidence despite 0-7 record
runners_data.comment: Close third of 11 at Newcastle last week suggests she could win a race like this
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 but last week's close third (Data Fata Secutus narrowly behind in fifth) of 11 at Newcastle (5f, AW) suggests she can win a race like this; showed promise on turf last summer; likely to go well.

runners_data.name: Riffa Spirit
runners_data.note: Only confirmed leader gets uncontested early advantage, 3lb claimer potentially costly in tight finish, 18 days off reasonable
runners_data.comment: Raced on AW, winning novice at two; fair fourth in handicap on return for new yard; claims
runners_data.spotlight: Raced on AW, winning 6f Chelmsford novice for the Crisfords last summer; led until well inside the final furlong when fourth of seven in 5f Southwell handicap on reappearance for new yard 18 days ago; if he comes on only a little for that outing he could take a bit of pegging back in this lower grade.

runners_data.name: Moretons
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but 11-race maiden tag concerning, recent Catterick efforts workmanlike without suggesting breakthrough imminent
runners_data.comment: 0-11 and not showing enough to suggest that a first win is imminent
runners_data.spotlight: 11-race maiden; not disgraced in 5f Catterick handicaps in recent weeks without suggesting a first win is imminent.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Terms
runners_data.note: Hold-up style needs pace collapse, recent Newcastle win over 6f questions stamina for sustained 5f gallop
runners_data.comment: Won over 6f latest but fact she got on top late doesn't suggest she's crying out for 5f
runners_data.spotlight: Left her first three efforts for Iain Jardine behind when winning over 6f at Newcastle 16 days ago; the way she got on top towards the finish doesn't suggest she's crying out for this drop to 5f for the first time but the fact she's a last-time-out winner counts for something.

runners_data.name: Realistic Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 91-day break with warning about fading in finish, new stable angle only positive
runners_data.comment: Well held in two Dundalk handicaps this winter but needs betting check for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field in two 6f handicaps at Dundalk for Andrew Slattery this winter but her new stable is no stranger to success with recruits from Ireland, including with its other runner here; one to note in the betting.

runners_data.name: Data Fata Secutus
runners_data.note: Previously pulled too hard but settled better last time, needs strong pace to maximize late kick
runners_data.comment: Some promise when close fifth of 11 on last week's Newcastle return; in the mix again
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled too hard in a pair 5f AW nurseries at Newcastle at the end of 2025 but settled better ridden with restraint on her recent reappearance there (5f again), keeping on to finish a close fifth of 11, with the reopposing Fille Unique third; entitled to come on for the run and should be on the premises.

runners_data.name: Gillali Lass
runners_data.note: Prominent style fits race shape well, 281-day absence major concern but O'Meara yard capable with returning horses

races.paceDynamic: Riffa Spirit is the only confirmed front-runner in this seven-horse field and should get an uncontested lead over this sharp 5f at Musselburgh. With Fille Unique, Moretons, and Gillali Lass likely to press forward but not challenge Riffa Spirit's early position, the pace should be honest but not suicidal. The hold-up horses Pivotal Terms, Realistic Dream, and Data Fata Secutus will need to rely on the pace collapsing in the final furlong. This race shape strongly favours the prominent racers who can track the leader without getting into an early speed duel.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Riffa Spirit gets soft fractions and isn't pressed early
scenarios.body: The front-runner controls the tempo and has enough left to repel late challenges, while prominent horses battle for the places. Riffa Spirit's recent Southwell fourth showed stamina when leading, making him hard to peg back if unopposed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but sustainable allowing tracking horses to pounce
scenarios.body: Fille Unique or Gillali Lass get perfect trips behind Riffa Spirit before swooping late over this speed-favouring track. Their prominent style gets them close enough without the workload of making the running.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Riffa Spirit goes too fast early or gets pressured by the prominent group
scenarios.body: The pace collapses dramatically in the final furlong allowing Pivotal Terms or Data Fata Secutus to storm home. Pivotal Terms' recent Newcastle win came with a strong finish that could translate to turf.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Opens Door
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses challenge Riffa Spirit early creating a fierce gallop
scenarios.body: Early speed horses tie up badly in the final 100 yards while a mid-division runner like Moretons or Realistic Dream picks up the pieces. This scenario requires tactical errors from prominent runners.

watchPoints.text: Riffa Spirit getting uncontested fractions through the first 2f as only natural leader could prove decisive advantage
Fille Unique's early positioning - if she settles kindly behind leader rather than fighting for lead she becomes major threat
Data Fata Secutus pulling hard early would compromise her finishing kick like in previous outings
Gillali Lass showing ring rustiness despite strong form before long absence
Pivotal Terms needing genuine strong pace to set up her hold-up style over this minimum trip

races.name: Edinburgh Rugby Handicap

runners_data.name: As Fast As Wind
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 233-day break with solid hurdles form suggesting retained fitness and stamina credentials.
runners_data.comment: In good form over hurdles since joining this yard and bold show likely back on the Flat
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 1m6f at Salisbury (good to soft) for Daisy Hitchins last summer; has been running creditably in defeat over hurdles since joining Tristan Davidson, including placed twice here; leading claims back on the Flat in a race where her rivals have something to prove.

runners_data.name: Glasses Up
runners_data.note: Veteran front-runner whose 12 career wins include hat-trick success, though 11 victories came at Ayr rather than this track.
runners_data.comment: Hit form last spring but has never won first time up in his long career
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran who has won here but 11 of his 12 career successes having been gained at Ayr, including a hat-trick last spring; well handicapped on those exploits but has never won first time up.

runners_data.name: Sycamore Gap
runners_data.note: Hold-up type switching back to turf after two disappointing all-weather runs for new trainer Stephen Hanlon.
runners_data.comment: Hasn't shown enough in two AW outings back from an absence to fancy his chances here
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark on AW at Newcastle (1m4f) in September 2024 on his final start for Rebecca Menzies but hasn't seriously threatened in two recent AW outings for new yard since returning from a long absence.

runners_data.name: Lieutenant Lily
runners_data.note: Ten-race maiden hold-up horse who showed promise at Newcastle but has been well beaten in recent efforts.
runners_data.comment: Some promise for new yard when sixth at Newcastle but well held at Southwell since
runners_data.spotlight: Ten-race maiden; some promise on second start for current yard when sixth over 1m2f at Newcastle last month but well beaten over 1m3f at Southwell since; placed on turf last year.

runners_data.name: Cougar
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won twice in blinkers last season but faded badly when racing without them most recently.
runners_data.comment: Won twice in blinkers last autumn; no blinkers when well held on return but back on now
runners_data.spotlight: Revitalised in blinkers and ended 2025 with victories over C&D (good to soft) and at Hamilton (1m4f, soft) in September; went without the blinkers when always behind on his Thirsk reappearance 11 days ago but could fare a lot better with the headgear back in place now.

runners_data.name: Blondina
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning to Flat after 327 days off and disappointing hurdles campaign for Adam Nicol.
runners_data.comment: Modest maiden on Flat in Ireland and well held in three hurdles for current yard
runners_data.spotlight: Modest maiden on the Flat in Ireland for Jim Bolger and has shown little in three hurdles for current yard this year; best watched back on the Flat unless the betting suggests otherwise.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing first-time cheekpieces after two poor Newcastle efforts this year.
runners_data.comment: Won off similar mark on AW in 2025 but well held both starts this year; new headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Came good off a similar mark at Newcastle (1m2f) last summer but well held in two outings there this year; his hopes are pinned on a change of headgear (first-time cheekpieces for blinkers) sparking a revival.

runners_data.name: Star Of Markinch
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up maiden ridden by 3lb claimer after failing to beat a rival on Newcastle reappearance.
runners_data.comment: Placed over C&D but is a longstanding maiden and failed to beat a rival on reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Placed several times (including C&D) but this 10yo remains a longstanding maiden and failed to beat a rival on her Newcastle reappearance seven weeks ago.

runners_data.name: Gallus Norman
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from nine-month absence but racing at realistic low handicap mark.
runners_data.comment: Well held in bumpers and on Flat but more chance now handicapping; check betting
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in two bumpers and three Flat runs at up to 1m3f last year but much more realistic chance now handicapping at a low level after nine months off; one to note in the betting.

races.paceDynamic: Glasses Up will dictate from the front with Falaise Blanc likely to race prominently, creating a sustainable early gallop over this stamina-testing trip. With only one confirmed front-runner and several hold-up horses, the pace will be steady rather than searching early, allowing the field to bunch up entering the home straight. The combination of good going, a stiff 1m4½f trip, and limited early pressure means horses with finishing speed will get their chance to close strongly. This race shape clearly favours hold-up performers who can stay the trip and produce a late kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Glasses Up sets modest fractions and the pace stays slow throughout
scenarios.body: The patient riders get perfect positioning and the race becomes a sprint finish where class and acceleration matter most. Several hold-up types can unleash late runs simultaneously.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Duo Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Glasses Up and Falaise Blanc work together and maintain strong gallop
scenarios.body: They get first run on the field and hold off late challenges through superior positioning and fitness advantages. The hold-up horses leave their runs too late on the testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is crawling and becomes tactical
scenarios.body: The race turns into a messy scramble where positioning and luck in running become crucial factors. Horses that can quicken from any position hold major advantages over pure stayers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Falaise Blanc pushes Glasses Up into faster fractions than ideal
scenarios.body: The sustained pace plays to genuine stayers and catches out horses that need to conserve energy for late kicks. Only the most robust hold-up horses survive the test.

watchPoints.text: Glasses Up could steal this if allowed uncontested lead, as veteran knows how to control fractions at this trip
Cougar's fading pattern suggests fitness concerns despite class advantage when blinkers were applied
As Fast As Wind's 233-day absence creates uncertainty despite solid recent hurdles form suggesting retained ability
Falaise Blanc's first-time cheekpieces could spark improvement after disappointing recent all-weather runs
Several hold-up horses may converge late creating traffic problems in home straight with limited racing room

races.name: Hibernian Community Foundation Handicap

runners_data.name: Sugar Hill Babe
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 187 days but has won fresh before and showed C&D ability previously
runners_data.comment: Returns on a winning mark and has gone well when fresh before
runners_data.spotlight: Reappears off the mark she defied at Nottingham (5f, good to firm) last May and has won first time up before; also a creditable third on previous C&D visit; no surprise were she to go well.

runners_data.name: Curious Rover
runners_data.note: Left impression last run would bring him on after leading long way before weakening at this track
runners_data.comment: Behind Al Hussar on C&D return but entitled to strip fitter now
runners_data.spotlight: Behind Al Hussar on his C&D reappearance 25 days ago but he did leave the impression the run would bring him on, weakening having led for a long way.

runners_data.name: Rosenpur
runners_data.note: Specialist around left-handed bends with five wins in 2025, near-miss last Wednesday suggests fitness intact
runners_data.comment: Had excellent 2025 and near miss on last week's return suggests 2026 can be productive too
runners_data.spotlight: Five wins, all around a left-hand bend (5f-5.5f), in a productive 2025 campaign; his near miss on 6f Catterick reappearance (good) last Wednesday suggests he's unlikely to be long in opening his account for 2026; same mark today.

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who disappointed on stable debut for new trainer, needs to prove the move works
runners_data.comment: C&D winner for Jim Goldie but always behind on C&D yard debut 17 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Scored three times, including over C&D, during his spell with Jim Goldie but always behind on C&D stable debut 17 days ago; can only watch after that.

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: Prolific winner but latest C&D effort was below par, hold-up style needs pace to aim at
runners_data.comment: Prolific winner, most recently on AW last month; latest C&D sixth was below par, though
runners_data.spotlight: Prolific winner, most recently on Wolverhampton AW last month; latest C&D sixth (Al Hussar third) of 15 wasn't one of his better efforts, though.

runners_data.name: Knicks
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who hasn't won for ages but showed encouragement on Thirsk reappearance 11 days ago
runners_data.comment: On losing run but reappearance encouraging and won the last time he wore cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: It's a long time since he won but he was a close third over C&D (good to soft) last September and was an encouraging sixth of 18 on reappearance at Thirsk (6f, good); refitted with cheekpieces (which are combined with his tongue-tie) for the first time since a win at Nottingham in autumn 2023; non-runner here on Sunday with a vet's certificate.

runners_data.name: Al Hussar
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with two solid C&D efforts this month, looks the pick of the backmarkers
runners_data.comment: Two solid efforts over C&D this month and likely to go well for in-form Grant Tuer.
runners_data.spotlight: Has returned with two solid efforts over C&D this month, latterly fourth of 17 to Montezuma (ran well again here on Sunday) on good to soft; likely to go well for in-form Grant Tuer.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with four 2025 wins but was tailed off last time on C&D reappearance
runners_data.comment: Four wins last year (including C&D) but last of 12 on C&D return over Easter
runners_data.spotlight: Four sprint wins in 2025 (including C&D) but hardly shaped as if her next win was imminent when last of 12 on C&D reappearance 25 days ago.

races.paceDynamic: Rosenpur will make the early running from his prominent style, likely accompanied by Sugar Hill Babe and Curious Rover in the vanguard. With only one confirmed front-runner in Rosenpur, the pace should be sustainable rather than frantic over this minimum trip. The majority of the field are hold-up horses (Jm Jhingree, Water Of Leith, Knicks, Al Hussar, Woohoo) who will need to be produced late. This setup creates a tactical advantage for the prominent runners who can sit closer to a moderate pace and have less ground to make up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Rosenpur sets a controlled tempo without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: The pace-setters can control the race from the front while the hold-up brigade get caught flat-footed behind a modest gallop. Rosenpur's recent Catterick near-miss and Sugar Hill Babe's C&D form make them hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with multiple prominent runners competing
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks as the leaders tire. Al Hussar's solid recent C&D form and Knicks's encouraging Thirsk return put them in the frame.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Rosenpur Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Rosenpur gets an uncontested lead and dictates throughout
scenarios.body: His five wins around left-handed bends this season suggest he can control from the front when unopposed. The hold-up horses struggle to reel in a horse who knows how to win from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot Breakthrough
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely or favorites underperform fitness-wise
scenarios.body: Water Of Leith's prolific winning record or Woohoo's four 2025 sprint wins could surface if the market leaders fail to deliver. Both have questions to answer after recent disappointing efforts.

watchPoints.text: Rosenpur breaks smartly and gets an uncontested lead - his left-handed bend record makes him very dangerous
Sugar Hill Babe travels kindly despite the 187-day layoff - previous fresh wins make her a live danger
Al Hussar gets cover in the pack early - his recent C&D form makes him the most reliable hold-up option
Curious Rover shows more early pace than last time when he led too long and weakened
Water Of Leith moves into contention turning for home - his class could surface if others disappoint

races.name: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Handicap

runners_data.name: Qazaq
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who was unlucky over course and distance last time, 17 days off ideal
runners_data.comment: Looked unlucky when close second over C&D latest; big player if showing up in similar form
runners_data.spotlight: Drawn a blank since winning first three starts for Roger Varian but surely would have put that right over C&D (good) last time with more luck in running, going down by only a head despite being repeatedly denied a run in the penultimate furlong; might need the breaks if he's dropped in from the outside stall but still has to be high on the list.

runners_data.name: Catalyse
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 95-day break for new connections, booking could be significant
runners_data.comment: Well held when backed on AW yard debut but remains one who could click for this stable
runners_data.spotlight: Never threatened when backed into 7-2 on his stable debut at Newcastle (6f) in January but remains one who could click for this yard and it will be interesting to see whether there is money for him again now back on turf after 95 days off.

runners_data.name: Mission Command
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer in good form, placed in last two turf starts
runners_data.comment: Now 15 runs since last win but arrives on the back of good thirds on turf in recent weeks
runners_data.spotlight: It's now 15 starts since his last success but he comes here in good nick, finishing third on turf at Pontefract (1m, good to soft) and Leicester (7f, good) in recent weeks.

runners_data.name: Counting Cards
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 107-day layoff, wore headgear last time
runners_data.comment: Took keen for own good on AW in the winter but claims if hood helps him to settle better
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who returned from an absence to finish runner-up off 2lb higher on his 1m Southwell handicap debut last October; too keen when failing to reproduce that form in two subsequent AW outings around the turn of the year but possible he could pack more punch at the finish if a first-time hood (combined with tongue-tie) helps him to settle better; runner-up on turf (good to firm) as a juvenile.

runners_data.name: Criminal Shore
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form, raced nine days ago so fitness assured
runners_data.comment: Drawn a blank since 1m Ripon win last April but several good efforts since
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win was at Ripon (1m, good) last April but he's run plenty of good races since; last week's fifth of 14 at Newcastle (7f) was another respectable effort but he remains 2lb above the mark he defied at Ripon.

runners_data.name: Giorgio M
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner using 5lb claimer, 29 days since last run may need this

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 213-day absence for trainer with limited recent runners
runners_data.comment: Promise for Katie Scott at end of last summer; off seven months (has had wind surgery)
runners_data.spotlight: 7f maiden win at Dundalk when trained by Kevin Coleman; placed on three of four starts for Katie Scott last August/September, including over C&D (good to soft); has had wind surgery ahead of this first start for seven months.

runners_data.name: Carolus Magnus
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist and course winner returning after 134-day break, proven here
runners_data.comment: Did well over C&D last autumn and claims if ready to roll after 134 days off
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner (good) last October; also runner-up off today's mark back here in November and could play a prominent role again if fully primed after 134 days off.

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Front-runner fresh from seven-day turnaround, still seeking first handicap success
runners_data.comment: Led for long way when third at Catterick last week and can figure prominently again
runners_data.spotlight: Still seeking a first handicap success but he went desperately close at Kempton (7f) last month; sound return to turf when third of nine at Catterick (7f, good) last Wednesday, leading for a long way; respected at a track which suits prominent racers.

runners_data.name: Penny Mountain
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare using 3lb claimer, lowest-rated but form figures suggest competitiveness
runners_data.comment: In good form on AW at Newcastle, placing over 7f last three starts; player back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Just one win from her 17 starts but that came on New Year's Day at Newcastle (6f) and she's largely continued in form there since, placing over 7f on her last three visits; raced only on AW for this yard but her peak RPR was achieved on turf in Ireland.

races.paceDynamic: Giorgio M and Tattie Bogle will dispute the early lead, with both confirmed front-runners likely to go a good clip from the start. Counting Cards and Criminal Shore should race prominently just behind the leaders, while the majority including Qazaq, Catalyse, Mission Command, Black Storm, Carolus Magnus and Penny Mountain will settle further back. The strong pace from Giorgio M and Tattie Bogle should create an honest gallop throughout, stretching the field and setting up a tactical battle. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can benefit from the strong early pace and finish with late runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Holds Up
scenarios.trigger: If Giorgio M and Tattie Bogle maintain their duel through halfway and beyond
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will stretch the field and favour those with finishing kicks from off the pace. Hold-up specialists like Qazaq and Mission Command can time their runs perfectly in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Leader Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Giorgio M or Tattie Bogle steals a march and gets first run on their rivals
scenarios.body: One of the front-runners capitalizes on tactical positioning and maintains momentum when the pace softens. The prominent runners struggle to peg back the leader's advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate and Giorgio M/Tattie Bogle don't establish clear dominance
scenarios.body: The race becomes more tactical with prominent runners able to track the leaders without pressure. Counting Cards and Criminal Shore can position perfectly for sustained drives.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Dash Specialist
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses completely and becomes crawling
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where pure speed matters most over tactical positioning. Those with the highest turn of foot regardless of running style can capitalize.

watchPoints.text: Giorgio M and Tattie Bogle must both show early speed or the pace scenario collapses entirely
Catalyse and Black Storm returning from long layoffs may need the run despite strong profiles
Qazaq's draw and early positioning will be crucial given his hold-up style and course form
Counting Cards showed keen tendencies last time which could compromise his prominent racing style
Mission Command's consistency makes him a reliable yardstick for the overall pace of the race

races.name: Racing TV Handicap

runners_data.name: Alpine Sierra
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong recent AW form who handles turf equally well and should get ideal position behind the leaders
runners_data.comment: Has gone close on AW on last three starts; obvious claims back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in AW handicaps on his last three starts, in the last two by narrow margins; equally as effective on turf, so has obvious claims for the track's top trainer.

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: Prominent type struggling for form since returning from absence with trainer out of sorts recently
runners_data.comment: Out of sorts since returning from an absence; major revival needed
runners_data.spotlight: Triple turf winner (7f/1m) but his last success was in August 2023 and he's been out of sorts since returning in September from a lengthy absence; mark is tumbling but he needs a major revival.

runners_data.name: Come On John
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 177-day break but showed glimpses of ability before losing form badly
runners_data.comment: Badly out of sorts when last seen in the autumn
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable fifth on AW last June on his first start for Alison Hamilton but lost his way badly in three subsequent outings; back from six months off and a leap of faith is needed.

runners_data.name: On The Bubble
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 190-day absence with solid course form but win record remains poor
runners_data.comment: Some fair efforts here in 2025 but 1-27 on Flat overall; off 190 days; others stronger
runners_data.spotlight: 1-27 on the Flat; some of last year's best efforts came here but she's still opposable for win purposes after 190 days off.

runners_data.name: Pallas Lord
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with Newcastle win credentials but turf form less convincing than AW exploits
runners_data.comment: Better known as an AW specialist but he has run well here before
runners_data.spotlight: Gained Newcastle win number ten in February; respectable sixth at Wolverhampton (8.6f) latest; it's hard to get excited by last year's turf exploits but he was runner-up over 1m here in April 2024.

runners_data.name: Esque Elegance
runners_data.note: Prominent type who finally broke maiden at Newcastle nine days ago and should be confident with same jockey
runners_data.comment: Made it 21st time lucky on AW last week; claims under a penalty if in similar form
runners_data.spotlight: Finally got off the mark at 21st time of asking when seeing off 13 rivals over 1m at Newcastle (AW) under Conor Whiteley nine days ago; should be very competitive under a 5lb penalty if showing up in a similar mood.

runners_data.name: Staffordshire
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won well at Newcastle in February and suits patient tactics from the rear
runners_data.comment: Came good on AW in February; saddle slipped since, so that run can be ignored
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark over 1m2f at Newcastle in February, pulling clear with a next-time-out winner; didn't get the chance to show what he could do back there next time (saddle slipped); probably acts on turf.

runners_data.name: Drumcondra
runners_data.note: Front-runner with course form including runner-up finish at this trip but poor effort last week at Beverley
runners_data.comment: Twice second here last year but needs to shrug off a lesser run at Beverley six days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up twice at this venue (including this trip) last term; needs to be in better form than he was at Beverley last week (seventh of nine) but it's possible that refitted blinkers will give him a lift.

runners_data.name: Miss Raincloud
runners_data.note: Hold-up type prone to fading in finish with first-time cheekpieces after 95-day break
runners_data.comment: Placed on AW last autumn but lost her way completely since; cheekpieces reached for
runners_data.spotlight: Exposed maiden who was placed over 7f/1m on AW last autumn but had lost her form completely when last seen in January; first-time cheekpieces (replacing hood) need to make a big difference.

races.paceDynamic: Pallas Lord and Drumcondra will set a solid pace from the gate, with Pallas Lord likely to edge ahead given his stronger front-running credentials. Four prominent runners (Alpine Sierra, Spirit Catcher, On The Bubble, Esque Elegance) will create congestion behind the leaders, potentially causing traffic problems approaching the home turn. The honest gallop set by the two leaders should create a true test over this 1m1f trip on good ground. This pace setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the early scrimmaging and finish with one run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack gets bunched up behind the dueling leaders
scenarios.body: The pace will be strong enough to set up the race for late closers who can pick their way through or around the field. Staffordshire and Come On John are perfectly positioned to exploit this scenario with their patient tactics.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Prevails Clean
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners can secure clear racing room turning for home
scenarios.body: Alpine Sierra or Esque Elegance can use their recent form advantage to strike in the final furlong. The good ground and honest pace will suit their style of tracking the pace before quickening.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Pallas Lord can establish a clear lead without pressure from Drumcondra
scenarios.body: His Newcastle win shows he retains ability, and if the prominent pack hesitates, he could steal a march turning for home. The good ground conditions suit his front-running style better than recent AW efforts.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If both Pallas Lord and Drumcondra fail to show early speed
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where any runner with tactical speed can win. This scenario would particularly suit any horse that can quicken from midfield positions.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems at the two-furlong pole where four prominent runners could get squeezed behind the leading pair
Drumcondra showed poor form at Beverley last week so may not provide the expected early pace pressure
Esque Elegance carries confidence from recent breakthrough win with same jockey partnership renewed
Come On John faces fitness questions after 177-day absence despite trainer change potentially helping
Staffordshire's patient running style could prove decisive if the pace holds up as expected

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with three wins from last four starts at Newcastle, proven at this course and distance
runners_data.comment: Has won three of last four on AW and escapes penalty for latest; C&D scorer
runners_data.spotlight: Made it three wins in his last four starts (all 6f at Newcastle) when seeing off ten rivals in an apprentice race last week; former C&D scorer so the step back up in trip shouldn't be an issue and he escapes a penalty.

runners_data.name: Filey Beach
runners_data.note: Only front runner who can dictate the pace without pressure, 19 days since disappointing effort may have needed the run
runners_data.comment: May have needed recent reappearance and did well over C&D last autumn
runners_data.spotlight: Did well over C&D for Ruth Carr last autumn; below par in three outings since, although two of those were for another yard, and he was entitled to need his recent first outing back with Ruth Carr after five months off; a return to form wouldn't surprise.

runners_data.name: Without Delay
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but wind surgery concerns after poor Redcar return last week
runners_data.comment: Well treated on last summer's form but down the field on recent reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Favourably handicapped on last summer's form but hard to draw any positives from last week's Redcar reappearance after wind surgery.

runners_data.name: Invincible Melody
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 0-23 record, needs significant pace collapse to feature from the rear
runners_data.comment: Well held at Thirsk this month on first run for Ewan Whillans, taking record to 0-23
runners_data.spotlight: Well held in 7f Thirsk handicap this month on his first start for Ewan Whillans, taking his record to 0-23.

runners_data.name: War Memorial
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner showing improvement with encouraging Southwell second seven weeks ago
runners_data.comment: Major step back in right direction when second latest; draw not ideal but still big player
runners_data.spotlight: Out the back on first four outings for Lawrence Mullaney but big step back in the right direction when second in 7f Southwell classified event seven weeks ago, pulling clear with one who has won and finished a close second in two handicap starts since; his last 11 outings have been on AW but was runner-up over C&D (good) in August 2024; bold show likely if a wide stall isn't too much of an inconvenience.

runners_data.name: Due Respect
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning from 227-day break without the first-time visor that sparked her only win
runners_data.comment: Came good in visor last July but out of sorts after; headgear left off on return
runners_data.spotlight: Came good in a first-time visor at Redcar (7f, good to soft) last July but the headgear didn't work as well in her three subsequent starts last year and is left off for her reappearance; others are more persuasive.

runners_data.name: Baby Rover
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose 5f Catterick run three weeks ago offers little hope over this longer trip
runners_data.comment: 6f win last summer but hard to draw any encouragement from recent reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 6f handicap at Redcar last summer; runner-up twice afterwards but didn't offer any obvious short-term encouragement on 5f Catterick reappearance three weeks ago; first 7f outing since finishing last on her course debut in 2024.

runners_data.name: Classy Clarets
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner better on AW recently, 5f last-time-out suggests connections unsure of best trip
runners_data.comment: In good form on AW in recent months, including 6f win; just as good at 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Back to form on AW for Iain Jardine in recent months, including 6f 0-50 classified win at Wolverhampton; found things happening too quickly for her over 5f in another classified event at Newcastle last time but kept on for a creditable third; 7f winner last year; one of two solid contenders for the yard.

runners_data.name: Gimmieminnie
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner prone to fading in finish, tough task from unfavoured tactical position
runners_data.comment: Fair start for new yard when fourth at Wolverhampton but well behind The Gay Blade since
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish; sold for 2,600gns to join current yard in January; fair effort when fourth of 11 in a classified on stable debut at Wolverhampton (6f) last month but well behind The Gay Blade at Newcastle last month; hood off, refitted tongue-tie and first-time cheekpieces combination on.

runners_data.name: Ridgemaster
runners_data.comment: 66-1 surprise win on Newcastle yard debut but well held there twice since; cheekpieces on
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled in six runs for Hugo Palmer but he sprang a 66-1 surprise on his 7f Newcastle stable debut in December; hasn't come close to backing that up in two subsequent outings; now fitted with first-time cheekpieces back on turf.

runners_data.name: Bernie The Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form came on AW for previous trainer Richard Fahey in 2023
runners_data.comment: All wins came on AW in 2023 and recent efforts don't suggest he'll snap losing run now
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins came on AW in 2023 when trained by Richard Fahey; only narrowly denied by The Gay Blade over 6f at Newcastle in February but hasn't been in same form since, including behind that reopposing rival there last week.

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with basement mark but 156 days off and poor recent efforts suggest he needs this
runners_data.comment: No obvious promise last year but has basement mark for handicaps and needs betting check
runners_data.spotlight: Beat only one home in three qualifying runs over sprint trips last autumn but has a basement mark as a result and his half-brother Ahamonent is a fair handicapper over this trip, including a course win; hooded first time; one to monitor in the betting.

races.paceDynamic: Filey Beach is the sole confirmed front runner and will take this field along at his own pace from the gates. The Gay Blade and Without Delay will track closely as prominent runners, but neither has the early pace to pressure Filey Beach in the opening stages. This creates a tactical advantage for the leader, who can dictate fractions without interference, while the large contingent of hold-up horses (War Memorial, Due Respect, Baby Rover, Classy Clarets, Gimmieminnie, Bernie The Bear, Approaching Dawn) will be bunched together seeking racing room in the straight. The uncontested lead and patient pace strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can position handy early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Filey Beach maintains a steady gallop without pressure through the first half-mile
scenarios.body: He can quicken clear turning for home before the hold-up brigade can mount their challenges. The patient fractions allow him to have enough left for the finish despite his moderate recent form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If The Gay Blade or Without Delay can sit perfectly behind Filey Beach and time their move
scenarios.body: They benefit from the pace scenario while having that crucial tactical edge over the hold-up horses who must come from further back. The Gay Blade's recent winning form gives him the edge in this battle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Comeback
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to set up the race for closers
scenarios.body: War Memorial's Southwell second or Classy Clarets' AW form could translate with a perfectly timed run. However, they need significant pace collapse to overcome their positioning disadvantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Filey Beach goes too slowly and gets swamped by everything in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The entire field converges in a messy finish where any horse can win on the day. This seems unlikely given the class gaps and form differentials in the field.

watchPoints.text: Filey Beach could steal this if allowed uncontested fractions - watch the opening two furlongs for any early pressure
The Gay Blade needs to position prominently from the gates given his style - poor beginning would compromise his chances significantly
Watch for any market moves on War Memorial given his improved Southwell effort and long absence since
Without Delay's breathing after wind surgery - any laboured action would confirm the Redcar effort wasn't just ring-rustiness
